name: eBay used bare A100 40GB SXM4 module (ex-datacenter pull, compliance-gated)
region: United States (seller in Eden Prairie, MN; listing marked US only)
price_basis: USED, BARE SXM4 MODULE with no host server, no baseboard, no heatsink/cooling shroud implied. $2,499.00 = listing 'NVIDIA 699-2G506-0200-310-V A100 40GB SXM4 HBM2 GPU', or Best Offer, captured 2026-10-03. NOTE the record points at the 80GB SXM4 accelerator family id because the repo has no separate A100 40GB record; the part being priced is the 40GB SXM4 variant. Warranty: none from NVIDIA; seller offers 30-day returns, buyer pays return shipping.
notes: The most useful anchor in the slice for 'what a single ex-datacenter A100 actually costs'. Seller condition text states it plainly: 'SXM4 Connection. US only. Requires Compliance Approval'. That clause is the norm, not the exception, on used SXM parts - export compliance gating is open and enforced, and a buyer without a compliance path cannot complete the sale. Free FedEx Ground. Seller Core 4 Solutions IT Hardware, 20,700 feedback. Cross-check from the same used-only A100 80GB query (2026-10-03): other bare 40GB SXM4 modules asked $2,499.95 / $2,899.00 / $2,929.99 / $2,999.97 / $3,149.99 / $3,354.99, and used 40GB PCIe cards $6,995-$8,074. So the SXM4 module trades at roughly HALF the used 40GB PCIe price - the form factor, not the silicon, drives the discount, because SXM needs a baseboard. RISK: burn-in and HBM error history are NOT disclosed on any of these listings; the 80GB PCIe listing at $12,500.00 has 'ECC Error' in its own title, which is the honest-disclosure case and rarer than it should be.
